title: Microsoft Teams: Copilot Chat in the Queues app Recap tab for recorded call queue calls
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, recording controls and published licence requirements match the sources checked. The changed recording documentation still supports the briefing, which reports the differing representative-assignment prerequisites and keeps queue-specific Copilot policy applicability and rollout defaults explicitly unresolved.

claims.quote: When enabled, all inbound call queue calls are automatically recorded when a representative (agent) answers.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Copilot calling-policy setting is documented for 1:1 Teams calls and PSTN calls.
claims.quote:
APPLIES TO: 1:1 Teams calls Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) calls
Use the Teams admin center or PowerShell to manage how users in your organization use Copilot in Teams calls.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Copilot reaches the Copilot calling-policy setting.
claims.quote:
Expand Voice from the navigation pane.
Under Voice, select Calling policies.
Either select an existing policy or create a new one.
From the dropdown for the Copilot setting, select On, On with saved transcript required, or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled turns off Copilot under the calling policy.
claims.quote:
To turn off Copilot for calls, use the following command:
Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not specifically establish whether that calling-policy setting governs Copilot on queue calls in the Queues app.
claims.quote: Searched: "Queues" "Copilot" "Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy" switch recap; opened Manage Microsoft Copilot in Teams calls and Queues app management; read calling-policy reference excerpts and Copilot release notes. No passage connected the policy to queue-call Recap.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The specific Recap feature's behaviour on arrival without administrator action is not stated, so its defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "Queues app" "Copilot" "default" "Recap"; read roadmap description, Copilot release-note entry, Manage Queues app and Copilot calling-policy pages. Product and calling-policy defaults are stated; the queue-call Recap feature's rollout default is not.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no Copilot-specific administrator switch for the Queues app Recap tab.
claims.quote: Searched: "Queues app" "Copilot" "Recap" admin policy default enabled licensing meter scope recorded calls; "Queues" "Copilot" "Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy" switch recap. Opened Queues app management, Copilot calling-policy and release-note pages; no Recap-only switch was documented.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe how this Copilot experience is permission-scoped to a queue call.
claims.quote: Searched: "Queues app" "Copilot" "scoped" "Recap"; read Copilot release notes, Queues app management and recording planning/setup pages. Recording access and Copilot availability are documented, but no queue-call Copilot permission-scoping mechanism is given.

claims.claim: The feature's release-note entry documents no actions taken on the user's behalf beyond answering and summarising.
claims.quote: Searched: "Queues app" "Copilot" "Recap" admin policy default enabled licensing meter scope recorded calls; opened and read the full queue-call entry in Copilot release notes. It describes opening Recap, requesting summaries and asking questions, not autonomous actions.
